chapter.h1: THE FIRST EPISTLE TO THE THESSALONIANS
chapter.li: LEChapter1 Verse1 Paul and Silvanus and Timothy, servants of God the Father and the Lord Jesus Christ, unto the church of the Thessalonians: Grace unto you, and peace from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ. VerseEnd

Verse2 We give thanks always, making mention of you all in our prayers to God for you, VerseEnd Verse3 remembering without ceasing your work of faith, and labor of love, and patience of hope in our Lord Jesus Christ, in the sight of God and our Father, VerseEnd Verse4 knowing, brethren beloved, your election of God. VerseEnd Verse5 For our gospel came not unto you in word only, but also in power, and in the holy ghost, and in much assurance, as you know what manner of men we were among you for your sake. VerseEnd Verse6 And you became imitators of us and of the Lord, having received the word in much affliction with joy of the holy ghost, VerseEnd Verse7 so that you were examples to all that believe in Macedonia and Achaia. VerseEnd Verse8 For from you sounded out the word of the Lord not only in Macedonia and Achaia, but also in every place your faith toward God is spread abroad, so that we need not to speak anything. VerseEnd Verse9 For they themselves show of us what manner of entrance in we had unto you, and how you turned to God from idols, to serve the living and true God VerseEnd Verse10 and to wait for his Son from Heaven, whom he raised from the dead, even Jesus, who delivered us from the wrath to come. VerseEnd

LEChapter2 Verse1 For you, brethren, know our entrance in unto you, that it was not in vain. VerseEnd Verse2 But even after we had suffered before and were shamefully treated, as you know, at Philippi, we were bold in our God to speak unto you the gospel of God, with much contention. VerseEnd Verse3 For our exhortation was not of deceit, nor of uncleanness, nor in guile, VerseEnd Verse4 but as we were approved of God to be entrusted with the gospel, even so we speak — not as pleasing men, but God, who tries our hearts. VerseEnd Verse5 For neither at any time used we flattering words, as you know, nor a cloak of covetousness — God is witness VerseEnd — Verse6 nor of men sought we glory, neither of you nor yet of others, when we might have been burdensome as the apostles of Christ. VerseEnd Verse7 But we were gentle among you, even as a nurse cherishes her children; VerseEnd Verse8 so being affectionately desirous of you, we were willing to have imparted unto you not the gospel of God only, but also our own souls, because you were dear unto us. VerseEnd

Verse9 For you remember, brethren, our labor and travail, laboring night and day because we would not be burdensome unto any of you, we preached unto you the gospel of God. VerseEnd Verse10 You are witnesses, and God also, how holily, and justly, and blamelessly we behaved ourselves among you that believe, VerseEnd Verse11 as you know how we exhorted and comforted and charged every one of you, as a father does his children, VerseEnd Verse12 that you would walk worthy of God, who has called you unto his kingdom and glory. VerseEnd

Verse13 For this cause also thank we God without ceasing, because when you received the word of God which you heard of us, you received it not as the word of men, but as it is in truth the word of God, which effectually works also in you that believe. VerseEnd Verse14 For you, brethren, became imitators of the churches of God which in Judea are in Christ Jesus; for you also have suffered like things of your own countrymen even as they have of the Jews, VerseEnd Verse15 who both killed the Lord Jesus and their own prophets, and have persecuted us; and they please not God and are contrary to all men, VerseEnd Verse16 forbidding us to speak to the Gentiles that they might be saved, to fill up their sins always; for the wrath is coming upon them to the utmost. VerseEnd

Verse17 But we, brethren, being taken from you for a short time in presence, not in heart, endeavored the more abundantly to see your face with great desire. VerseEnd Verse18 Wherefore, we would have come unto you, even I, Paul, once and again, but Satan hindered us. VerseEnd Verse19 For what is our hope, or joy, or crown of rejoicing? Are not even you, in the presence of our Lord Jesus Christ at his coming? VerseEnd Verse20 For you are our glory and joy. VerseEnd

LEChapter3 Verse1 Wherefore, when we could no longer bear it, we thought it good to be left at Athens alone VerseEnd Verse2 and sent Timothy, our brother and minister of God and our fellow laborer in the gospel of Christ, to establish you and to comfort you concerning your faith, VerseEnd Verse3 that no man should be moved by these afflictions. For you know that we are appointed unto this; VerseEnd Verse4 for truly, when we were with you, we told you before that we should suffer tribulation, even as it came to pass, and you know. VerseEnd Verse5 For this cause, when I could no longer bear it, I sent to know your faith, lest by some means the tempter have tempted you and our labor should be in vain. VerseEnd

Verse6 But now when Timothy came from you unto us and brought us good tidings of your faith and charity, and that you have good remembrance of us always, desiring greatly to see us as we also to see you, VerseEnd Verse7 therefore, brethren, we were comforted concerning you in all our affliction and distress by your faith. VerseEnd Verse8 For now we live, if you stand fast in the Lord. VerseEnd Verse9 For what thanks can we render to God again for you for all the joy with which we rejoice for your sakes before our God, VerseEnd Verse10 night and day praying exceedingly that we might see your face and might perfect that which is lacking in your faith? VerseEnd

Verse11 Now God himself, our Father, and our Lord Jesus Christ direct our way unto you. VerseEnd Verse12 And the Lord make you to increase and abound in love one toward another and toward all men, even as we do toward you, VerseEnd Verse13 to the end he may establish your hearts blameless in holiness before God, even our Father, at the coming of our Lord Jesus Christ with all his saints. VerseEnd

LEChapter4 Verse1 Furthermore then, we implore you, brethren, and exhort you by the Lord Jesus, that as you have received of us how you ought to walk and to please God, so you would abound more and more. VerseEnd Verse2 For you know what commandments we gave you by the Lord Jesus. VerseEnd Verse3 For this is the desire of God, even your sanctification; that you should abstain from fornication; VerseEnd Verse4 that every one of you should know how to possess his vessel in sanctification and honor VerseEnd — Verse5 not in the lust of licentiousness, even as the Gentiles who know not God; VerseEnd Verse6 that no man go beyond and defraud his brother in any matter, because the Lord is the avenger of all such, as we also have forewarned you and testified. VerseEnd Verse7 For God has not called us unto uncleanness, but unto holiness. VerseEnd Verse8 He therefore that despises, despises not man, but God, who has also given unto us his holy spirit. VerseEnd

Verse9 But as touching brotherly love, you need not that I write unto you, for you yourselves are taught of God to love one another, VerseEnd Verse10 and indeed you do it toward all the brethren who are in all Macedonia. But we implore you, brethren, that you increase more and more, VerseEnd Verse11 and that you strive to be quiet, and to do your own business, and to work with your own hands as we commanded you, VerseEnd Verse12 that you may walk honestly toward them that are outside and that you may have lack of nothing. VerseEnd

Verse13 But I would not have you to be ignorant, brethren, concerning them who are asleep, that you sorrow not, even as others who have no hope. VerseEnd Verse14 For if we believe that Jesus died and rose again, even so they also who sleep in Jesus will God bring with him. VerseEnd Verse15 For this we say unto you by the word of the Lord: that they who are alive at the coming of the Lord shall not precede them who remain unto the coming of the Lord who are asleep. VerseEnd Verse16 For the Lord himself shall descend from Heaven with a shout, with the voice of the archangel, and with the trump of God. And the dead in Christ shall rise first. VerseEnd Verse17 Then they who are alive shall be caught up together into the clouds with them who remain, to meet the Lord in the air, and so shall we be ever with the Lord. VerseEnd Verse18 Wherefore, comfort one another with these words. VerseEnd

LEChapter5 Verse1 But of the times and the seasons, brethren, you have no need that I write unto you, VerseEnd Verse2 for you know perfectly that the day of the Lord so comes: as a thief in the night. VerseEnd Verse3 For when they shall say, Peace and safety, then sudden destruction comes upon them as travail upon a woman with child, and they shall not escape. VerseEnd Verse4 But you, brethren, are not in darkness that that day should overtake you as a thief. VerseEnd Verse5 You are all the children of light and the children of the day. We are not of the night, nor of darkness; VerseEnd Verse6 therefore, let us not sleep, as do others, but let us watch and be sober. VerseEnd Verse7 For they that sleep in the night, and they that are drunk are drunk in the night. VerseEnd Verse8 But let us, who are of the day, be sober, putting on the breastplate of faith and love, and for a helmet, the hope of salvation. VerseEnd Verse9 For God has not appointed us to wrath, but to obtain salvation by our Lord Jesus Christ VerseEnd Verse10 who died for us, that whether we wake or sleep, we should live together with him. VerseEnd Verse11 Wherefore, comfort yourselves together and edify one another, even as also you do. VerseEnd

Verse12 And we implore you, brethren, to know them who labor among you and are over you in the Lord and admonish you, VerseEnd Verse13 and to esteem them very highly in love for their work’s sake. And be at peace among yourselves. VerseEnd Verse14 Now we exhort you, brethren: warn them that are unruly, comfort the feeble-minded, support the weak, be patient toward all men. VerseEnd Verse15 See that none render evil for evil unto any man, but ever follow that which is good, both among yourselves and to all men. VerseEnd Verse16 Rejoice for ever. VerseEnd Verse17 Pray without ceasing. VerseEnd Verse18 In everything give thanks, for this is the will of God in Christ Jesus concerning you. VerseEnd Verse19 Quench not the spirit. VerseEnd Verse20 Despise not prophesyings. VerseEnd Verse21 Prove all things; hold fast that which is good. VerseEnd Verse22 Abstain from all appearance of evil. VerseEnd Verse23 And the very God of peace sanctify you wholly, and I pray God your whole spirit and soul and body be preserved blameless unto the coming of our Lord Jesus Christ. VerseEnd Verse24 Faithful is he that calls you, who also will do it. VerseEnd

Verse25 Brethren, pray for us. VerseEnd Verse26 Greet all the brethren with a holy salutation. VerseEnd Verse27 I charge you by the Lord that this epistle be read unto all the holy brethren. VerseEnd Verse28 The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with you. Amen. VerseEnd

p.i: The first epistle unto the Thessalonians was written from Athens.
